questions.q: What does LoRA do with the model's original weights during training?
options: Freezes them entirely and never updates them
Updates them directly, same as full fine-tuning
Deletes and replaces them with random values
Compresses them into a smaller model first
questions.explain: The original weight matrix W is frozen; only the small added matrices B and A are trained.

questions.q: What does LoRA actually train, instead of the full weight matrix?
options: A complete second copy of the model
Two small low-rank matrices whose product approximates the change a full fine-tune would make
Only the model's tokenizer
The system prompt
questions.explain: The small matrices B and A are trained; their product (B·A) is added on top of the frozen weight as a learned detour.

questions.q: Why can a LoRA adapter be stored in megabytes instead of gigabytes?
options: It only works on very small models
It stores a lossy compressed copy of the whole model
It only contains the small trained matrices, not the full set of model weights
It is deleted automatically after training
questions.explain: An adapter only holds the small trained B and A matrices — not a copy of the (frozen, shared) base model's full weights.

questions.q: What does the rank (r) hyperparameter control in LoRA?
options: The number of training examples required
How many epochs training runs for
The base model's context window size
The size of the bottleneck dimension — capacity to learn vs. parameter efficiency
questions.explain: A higher rank gives the adapter more capacity to learn, at the cost of more parameters and less of LoRA's efficiency advantage.

questions.q: What does "merging" a LoRA adapter mean?
options: Combining two separate base models into one
Deleting the adapter after use
Folding the trained B·A update back into the base weights for zero extra inference latency
Averaging several adapters together automatically
questions.explain: Merging folds the adapter's learned update directly into the original weight matrix, so inference has no extra overhead compared to a normal fine-tuned model.
